papers.title_in_file: Myths around quantum computation before full fault tolerance: What no-go theorems rule out and what they don't
papers.what_it_is: A perspective article that argues the asymptotic no-go results on error mitigation and variational algorithms do not rule out useful near-term quantum computing.

assertions.value: The authors argue that exponential sampling-cost scaling of error mitigation does not by itself make error mitigation useless.
quotes: Thus, the fact that error mitigation methods scale exponentially does not mean that they are, per definition, useless.
assertions.certainty_reason: An argument in a perspective article, with no new experiment or proof in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that their numerical estimates of barren-plateau gradient probabilities rest on a crude extrapolation, and that they treat it as an open question whether good-gradient trajectories can be found in practice.
quotes: We stress that these numbers are based on a crude numerical extrapolation
It remains an open question whether or not such trajectories can be found in practice.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the limit of its estimate (Myth 4 discussion, p.5).

assertions.value: The authors report, citing other work, that in the standard cases that provably avoid barren plateaus the resulting training process is in a sense classically simulable.
quotes: it has recently been argued that in all those standard cases (that can be proven to avoid them) the resulting training process is in a sense classically simulable
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to a cited reference.

assertions.value: The authors state that achieving practical quantum advantage is highly nontrivial, partly because of hardware noise and the hardness of circuit training.
quotes: Achieving practical quantum advantage is highly nontrivial, partly due to limitations posed by hardware noise and due to the fundamental hardness of circuit training.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement in a perspective article.

papers.title_in_file: SEQUENT: Towards Traceable Quantum Machine Learning using Sequential Quantum Enhanced Training
papers.what_it_is: A paper that proposes a two-step classical-then-quantum training scheme for hybrid quantum transfer learning so the quantum part's impact can be traced.

assertions.value: The authors argue formally that in a dressed quantum circuit the quantum layer can represent the identity, so the network can approximate polynomial functions (the paper states a degree restriction that the quote does not reproduce) even if the variational circuit does not affect the prediction.
assertions.anchor: Section 4, Eq. 6 and following text, p.4
quotes: By the universal function approximation theorem, this allows DQC to approximate any polynomial function
assertions.certainty_reason: A short formal argument by the authors, not a numbered theorem; the coordinator may judge it differently.

assertions.value: The authors report test accuracies on the moons data set of 97% for SEQUENT, 95% for the dressed quantum circuit and 96% for the classical model, with an overall best accuracy of 86% on the spirals data set.
quotes: With a final test accuracy of 95%, the DQC performs even worse than the purely classical model reaching 96%.
Looking at the SEQUENT results however, these concerns are eliminated, as the performance and final accuracy of 97%,
The overall best accuracy of 86% however suggests, that further adjustments to the VQC could be beneficial.
assertions.certainty_reason: A single preliminary experiment on two toy data sets.
assertions.reader_inference: The accuracy differences are one to two points on toy data with no variance reported.

assertions.value: The authors state that they considered only a simple circuit with fixed angle embeddings, supplied only preliminary experimental results, and did not test high-dimensional real-world applications.
quotes: Furthermore, we only supplied preliminary experimental implications and did not yet test any high dimensional real-world applications.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope and limits (Section 7, p.7).

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning for Material Synthesis and Hardware Security (Invited Paper)
papers.what_it_is: An invited paper that applies a quantum LSTM to chemical retrosynthesis and a quantum neural network to hardware Trojan detection, in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report 65% training accuracy for QLSTM against 100% for a classical LSTM on retrosynthesis, and 80% testing accuracy for QLSTM against a 70% peak for the classical LSTM.
quotes: We achieve 65% training accuracy with QLSTM whereas classical LSTM can achieve 100%.
However, in testing we achieve 80% accuracy with the QLSTM while classical LSTM peaks at only 70% accuracy!
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on a small data subset.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper's own text says the classical accuracy falls during testing, which may reflect overfitting on small data rather than a quantum advantage.

assertions.value: The authors report that their QNN reached detection accuracy as high as 97.27% on hardware Trojan detection, and that it performed identically to a classical neural network, which produced 97.09%.
quotes: The QNN model achieves detection accuracy as high as 97.27%.
The QNN model performed identical to classicalNN, which produced an accuracy of 97.09%.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the goal of the work is not superior classification accuracy over classical counterparts but a proof-of-concept application of QML in the hardware security domain.
quotes: It should be noted that the goal of this work is not to demonstrate superior classification accuracy over classical counterparts, but rather to show a proof-of-concept application of QML in hardware security domain.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope (Section 4.4).

papers.title_in_file: Hierarchical quantum embedding by machine learning for large molecular assemblies
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusions, and the discussion of results; the theory and computational-details sections were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A computational chemistry paper that uses projection-based quantum-in-quantum embedding and transfer learning of a classical machine-learning potential to estimate a protein-ligand binding free energy.

assertions.value: The authors report that the machine-learning potential refined by transfer learning from the embedding data gave a binding free energy in close agreement with the experimental estimate and improved on their previous approach.
quotes: provided a binding free energy for MCL1-19G in close agreement with the experimental estimate
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one protein-ligand complex.
assertions.reader_inference: The quantum here is quantum chemistry on classical computers; the paper does not run quantum hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that training with only energies increased the errors for the forces, and conclude that energy derivatives are key for efficient training of the machine-learning potentials.
quotes: Training with only energies increased the errors for the forces
This demonstrates that energy derivatives are key for the efficient training of MLPs
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that analytical energy derivatives for highly accurate electronic structure methods within embedding frameworks are currently unavailable.
quotes: within embedding frameworks, which are, however, currently unavailable
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit (Section 5).

papers.title_in_file: NoRA: A Tensor Network Ansatz for Volume-Law Entangled Equilibrium States of Highly Connected Hamiltonians
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section structure and outlook; the numerical-study and appendix derivations were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that proposes a non-local tensor network ansatz and studies its random-Clifford case as a family of stabilizer codes.

assertions.value: The authors introduce a family of SYK-inspired codes that can be chosen to have constant rate and linear distance at the cost of some high-weight stabilizers.
quotes: We introduce a family of codes inspired by the SYK model which can be chosen to have constant rate and linear distance at the cost of some high weight stabilizers.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result from numerical study of random Clifford networks, not stated as a theorem.

assertions.value: The authors state that, without additional structure, the networks cannot be efficiently contracted on a classical computer.
quotes: However, without the imposition of additional structure it is not possible to efficiently contract these networks on a classical computer.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit (Section 1).

assertions.value: The authors argue the architecture is potentially expressive enough to capture the entanglement and complexity of the SYK ground space, and state that a detailed study of SYK is left to future work.
quotes: We argue that the architecture is potentially expressive enough to capture the entanglement and complexity of the ground space of the SYK model, thus making it a suitable variational ansatz, but we leave a detailed study of SYK to future work.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author argument; the paper says it did not test it on SYK.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum vs. classical: A comprehensive benchmark study for predicting time series with variational quantum machine learning
papers.what_it_is: A benchmark of variational quantum models against classical models for time series forecasting on three chaotic systems, run in noise-free simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state they evaluated predictive performance on three chaotic systems across 27 time series prediction tasks and ensured a fair comparison through extensive hyperparameter optimization.
quotes: We evaluate their predictive performance on three chaotic systems across 27 time series prediction tasks of varying complexity, and ensure a fair comparison through extensive hyperparameter optimization.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup (Abstract).

assertions.value: The authors report that variational QML methods generally perform at best on par with simple classical machine learning models across a broad range of prediction tasks.
quotes: Our findings indicate that variational QML methods generally perform at best on par with simple classical machine learning models across a broad range of prediction tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical benchmark result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the quantum models with the highest predictive performance often rely on a substantial number of classical trainable parameters.
quotes: Notably, the quantum models that achieve the highest predictive performance often rely on a substantial number of classical trainable parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical benchmark result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the benchmark calculations were performed under idealized conditions, without accounting for hardware limitations or finite-sampling noise.
quotes: The benchmark calculations in this work are performed under idealized conditions, without accounting for hardware limitations or finite-sampling noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit (Section VI).

papers.title_in_file: Towards AutoQML: A Cloud-Based Automated Circuit Architecture Search Framework
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, architecture, the qGAN use case and results, and conclusion; figure-only content not read.
papers.what_it_is: A framework paper that proposes a cloud architecture for parallel hyperparameter search of quantum machine learning models, demonstrated on a quantum GAN for energy prices.

assertions.value: The authors propose a cloud-based solution that enables distributed execution of experiments, results post-processing, parameter benchmarking and plot generation.
quotes: We propose a cloud-based solution that enables the distributed execution of experiments, results post-processing, parameter benchmarking and plot generation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own design and setup (Section II.A).

assertions.value: The authors report that, for a 5-qubit Zoufal ansatz on the energy price distribution, the best 5 qubit model selected was the uniform 2-layer with gate depth 77.
assertions.anchor: Section IV.B and Table I, p.5
quotes: The best 5 qubit model selected is the uniform 2-layer with gate depth 77 (bolded).
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the brute-force combinatorial approach to model parallelization and training should be simplified.
quotes: The brute-force combinatorial approach to model parallelization and training should be simplified.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its first version (Section V).

papers.title_in_file: Hamiltonian learning from time dynamics using variational algorithms
papers.what_it_is: A paper that reconstructs 2-local Hamiltonians and learns quantum states from time-series observables using variational circuits, tested in Qiskit simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that they present Hamiltonian learning for various 2-local Hamiltonians and state learning of quantum systems comprising up to 6 qubits.
quotes: We presented a comprehensive list of results corresponding to the Hamiltonian learning of various 2-local Hamiltonians as well as state learning of quantum systems comprising up to 6 qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope (Section 4).

assertions.value: The authors claim that their formalism rests on variational optimization with shallow-depth quantum circuits and is easily implementable on a near-term quantum device.
quotes: the entire workhorse of our proposed formalism is centered around variational optimization using shallow-depth quantum circuits and thus, is easily implementable on a near-term quantum device
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the results are numerical simulations.

assertions.value: The authors state that, given sufficient observables to characterize the dynamics of a Hamiltonian, they can uniquely converge on reconstructing the exact Hamiltonian.
quotes: given sufficient observables to characterize the dynamics of a Hamiltonian, we can uniquely converge on reconstructing the exact Hamiltonian.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim supported by numerical examples.
